title: Power out
steps: Check if it's just you. Report it to the utility.
Keep the fridge and freezer closed. Fridge food is safe about 4 hours, a full freezer about 48.
Generator outside only, at least 20 ft from doors and windows.
Unplug electronics. Follow your plan's first-2-hours checklist.

detail.title: 0 to 2 hours: Lock in water
items: Fill tubs and every pot while pressure lasts

detail.title: 2 to 24 hours: Set up camp
items: Solar up: freezer and a fan first

detail.title: Weeks 3 to 13: Long haul
items: Weekly drills of your exit plan

empty: Add your generators and batteries in My Place (type: Equipment), and the breaker panel as a Place.

title: Tornado warning
steps: Go to the lowest floor, an interior room with no windows (closet, bathroom, under stairs).
Get under something sturdy. Cover your head and neck with arms, a mattress or helmets.
In a car or mobile home: get out to a sturdy building. Last resort: a low ditch, covering your head.
Stay there until the warning expires. Then watch for downed lines and gas smells.
empty: Add your tornado safe room in My Place (type: Shelter, kind: tornado safe room).

title: Flash flood
steps: Move to higher ground now. Don't wait for an order.
Turn around, don't drown: 6 inches of moving water knocks you down, 12 inches floats a car.
Never drive into water over a road or through an underpass.
If trapped in a building, go to the highest floor. Only go on the roof if water keeps rising. Don't climb into a closed attic.
empty: Add your routes and flood spots in My Place (type: Route, or Place kind: flood spot).

title: Extreme heat
steps: Get everyone into the coolest room. Close sun-facing blinds.
Drink water often. Wet cloths on the neck and wrists, fan if possible.
Check older people, kids and pets every hour.
Heat stroke (confused, 103°F+, hot skin) is an emergency: cool them fast.

detail.title: Heat exhaustion: do
items: Loosen clothes, wet cloths on skin
Worse, or no better in 1 hour: treat as heat stroke

detail.title: Heat stroke: do
items: Get help if any is reachable
Cool them fast: cold water, ice packs to neck, armpits, groin, fan them

title: Hard freeze
steps: Everyone in one warm room. Close off the rest of the house.
Never use a grill, camp stove or generator indoors (carbon monoxide).
Drip faucets. Know where the main water shutoff is in case a pipe bursts.
Dress in layers, hats on, warm sweet drinks for anyone shivering.
keywords: cold snow ice pipes heat carbon monoxide

detail.title: Hypothermia
items: Get everyone into one warm room
Dry clothes, blankets, hats, warm sweet drinks if awake
Shivering stops while still cold: emergency

detail.title: Carbon monoxide
items: No grill, camp stove, charcoal or generator indoors or in the garage
Generator at least 20 ft out, exhaust away from windows
Headache, nausea, confusion in several people: get outside now
Battery CO alarms in every sleeping area

title: Fire or smoke
steps: Fire in the house: get out, stay out, call 911.
Wildfire smoke: stay inside, close windows, run a HEPA or box-fan filter.
Evacuation order: leave now with your go-bags. Don't wait to see the fire.
N95 masks help with smoke. Cloth masks don't.
empty: Add your exits and meeting point in My Place, and a clean-air center if you know one.

title: Boil-water notice or no water
steps: Boil notice: boil 1 minute (3 minutes above 6,500 feet), or use 8 drops of 6% bleach per gallon, wait 30 min.
Do-not-use notice: don't boil it (boiling can concentrate chemicals). Use stored water.
Shut the main valve if a line broke. Switch to your water ledger.
See Learn → Make water safe.

empty: Add your water shutoff in My Place with a photo

title: Radiation or chemical release
steps: Get inside. The nearest solid building. Go to the basement or the middle of the building, away from windows.
Stay inside. Close windows and doors. Turn off fans, AC and heat that pull in outside air. Stay put until officials say it's safe, usually at least 24 hours.
Stay tuned. NOAA weather radio, local AM/FM or TV. Follow official instructions over anything saved in this app.
source: CDC "Get Inside, Stay Inside, Stay Tuned" (radiation emergencies)

title: We need to leave
steps: Grab go-bags, meds, IDs, phone chargers, pets.
Text your out-of-area contact where you're going.
Use your saved routes. Avoid low crossings.
Leave a note on the door: who, where, when.

detail.title: Leave now if
items: Fire, smoke or a gas smell
CO alarm plus headache, nausea or confusion
Heat stroke signs and cooling isn't working
Flooding in the house or street
Indoors above 90°F day and night with a child, elder or sick person
Indoors below 50°F and the heat plan failed
Water is out and no source in reach
A medicine runs out and nothing is open
Threats or looting you can't handle

title: Someone is hurt
steps: M. Massive bleeding. Hard direct pressure. Limb spurting or soaking through: tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound, tight until bleeding stops. Write the time on it.
A. Airway. Talking means the airway is open. If not: head tilt, chin lift. Unconscious and breathing: recovery position on their side.
R. Respiration. Watch the chest rise. Chest wound with air sucking in: cover it with plastic taped on 3 sides.
C. Circulation. Pale, cold, sweaty, fast pulse means shock. Lay flat, raise legs if no spine injury, keep warm. Not breathing: start CPR.
H. Hypothermia and head. Keep them warm even in mild weather. Watch for confusion, vomiting or unequal pupils after a head hit.
source: Stop the Bleed and TCCC "MARCH" order
